featured_reviews.name: ritika ahuja

I visited Dr. Hemant for blurred vision and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience.

Upon arrival, the assistant conducted a standard vision test and informed me that my vision was perfect as I was able to read even the smallest letters. A pressure test was also performed, and I was told that the results were normal.

After this, I was repeatedly asked whether anyone in my family had glaucoma. I clearly stated that no one in my family has a history of glaucoma. Despite being told that my initial tests appeared normal, I was advised to undergo additional tests costing approximately ₹2,400 each. After those tests, I was again informed that the reports looked normal, yet I was asked to undergo two more tests costing another ₹2,400 each because the doctor "wanted more clarity." At this stage, my bill had already reached around ₹11,600.

I requested to meet the doctor before proceeding further and was eventually allowed to do so. During the consultation, I felt that my concerns regarding blurred vision were not adequately addressed. When I repeatedly asked what was causing my symptoms, I was mostly told that I was anxious and overthinking. I was reassured that I would not go blind, but I did not receive a clear explanation of my diagnosis.

What confused me further was that I was prescribed Thyronorm 25 mcg despite informing the doctor that I do not have a thyroid condition. My thyroid reports were normal, yet I was advised to take the medication for two days without a clear explanation of why it was necessary.

I was then told to return after two days for pupil dilation and further examination, along with an additional consultation charge. I questioned why this could not be done during the same visit, especially after already undergoing multiple expensive tests, but no satisfactory explanation was provided.

The post-consultation experience was equally frustrating. The prescription did not mention when to take the prescribed medication, and I was advised to WhatsApp the doctor for clarification. Despite following up multiple times, I did not receive a timely response. I also requested copies of my reports but was told that the printer was not working. However, I observed other documents being printed during my visit. More than five days later, I still had not received all my reports as promised.

Another concern was the pricing of the tests. After my visit, I checked with other centres and found that similar tests are often charged between ₹900 and ₹1,200. This left me questioning why I was charged significantly higher amounts without a clear explanation.

I fully understand that specialist consultations and advanced diagnostics can be expensive when medically justified. However, as a patient, I felt pressured into undergoing multiple tests before receiving a proper explanation of my condition. The lack of transparency, poor communication, difficulty obtaining reports, and inadequate follow-up made this a very disappointing experience.

I hope this feedback encourages greater transparency, clearer communication with patients, and better post-consultation support in the future.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an unpleasant experience with Dr Jatin Ashar. I visited with my father to inquire about getting lens, but the doctor insisted on LASIK surgery instead. When my father asked if the procedure was covered under CGHS, the doctor responded rudely and irritably, saying, "Har cheez CGHS ke andar nahi aata" (Not everything comes under CGHS). When my father mentioned that we could not afford the surgery, the doctor dismissed us immediately.

The doctor’s rude and dismissive behaviour felt unprofessional and gave the impression that the focus was more on money than on providing patient care.

Edit -

Thank you for your response. I would like to clarify a few things further:

1. Regarding the insistence on surgery:
While I appreciate your clarification, the fact remains that my initial query was regarding lenses, not surgery. The suggestion of LASIK surgery was made without taking my actual concern into consideration, which felt like an insistence on a different treatment.

2. Conveying information about CGHS coverage:
I understand that you were sharing a fact about CGHS coverage. However, the way it was conveyed—specifically the eye-roll and the tone—felt rude and dismissive. A simple fact can be stated in a respectful and professional manner, without conveying irritation. My concern is not about the fact itself but the delivery.

3. Dismissing us after mentioning affordability:
When my father expressed that we could not afford the surgery, the immediate dismissal of us from the consultation felt unprofessional. Instead of discussing alternative options or even providing some guidance, we were effectively shown the door. This is what I meant by being dismissed.

4. False promises or commitments:
While I agree that false promises should not be made, professionalism involves handling all patients with respect and care, especially when they raise concerns. In our case, the conversation could have been handled with more patience and understanding, and alternatives could have been suggested instead of just ending the interaction.

5. Professionalism and respect:
I believe professionalism goes beyond just giving facts; it also includes how we make patients feel during consultations. In this instance, the interaction left us feeling dismissed rather than respected or valued as patients. A more considerate and understanding approach would have made a positive difference.

Edit 2 -

It’s quite surprising to see how delusional one can be. At no point did I claim that Dr Ashar discussed charges or financial solutions with us. My concern was about his dismissive attitude and the way he handled our query.

Firmness and being straight to the point are not the issues here. The problem is the lack of courtesy and professionalism displayed during the interaction. Rolling one’s eyes, speaking irritably, and dismissing patients when they express financial constraints are not examples of firmness—they are examples of rude behaviour.

If you are unwilling to acknowledge this, that’s your prerogative, but dismissing genuine concerns as a misunderstanding or misrepresentation reflects poorly on the ability to take accountability.

Lastly, your attempt to redirect me to a counsellor for further assistance misses the point entirely. This is not about needing financial advice or further treatment—it’s about the lack of respect shown to patients during a consultation.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Looks like you have made up your mind that firmness and being straight to the point is being rude and unprofessional. Just to clarify that Dr Ashar never discusses any charges with any patients. We have a separate team of counsellors who do that. And he firmly refuses to talk about money matters or giving any financial solutions as he can only give medical advise and not financial advise to anyone. Please feel free to contact our counsellors if you need any further help with your treatment part.
